content_voiceover: Warm AIHA is IgG mediated and this diagram shows exactly how it destroys red cells. IgG antibodies coat the red cell surface at body temperature. Macrophages in the spleen recognize the Fc portion of IgG through Fc receptors and either engulf the entire cell — complete phagocytosis — or bite off just a piece of membrane, creating a microspherocyte that circulates with reduced surface area and increased osmotic fragility. This Fc-receptor mediated phagocytosis in the spleen is the dominant mechanism, and it's why splenectomy is a treatment option for refractory warm AIHA. IgG can also fix complement, though less efficiently than IgM, activating C1 through C4 and C3, generating C3b-coated red cells that are cleared by Kupffer cells in the liver via extravascular hemolysis. So for boards, the key takeaway is warm AIHA equals IgG, extravascular hemolysis, primarily in the spleen through Fc-receptor phagocytosis, producing spherocytes on peripheral smear, and a positive direct antiglobulin test for IgG, with or without complement.
keypoints: Fc-receptor mediated phagocytosis by splenic macrophages
Extravascular hemolysis (spleen > liver); DAT+ for IgG ± C3
keypoint_voiceover: Warm AIHA is driven by IgG coating red cells at body temperature. Splenic macrophages use Fc receptors to phagocytose these cells, either whole or in part, and partial bites create microspherocytes, the classic smear finding. This is extravascular hemolysis, mainly in the spleen, and the direct antiglobulin test is positive for IgG, sometimes with complement too.
